subject: GreenVault discovery: reliability & graceful-degradation recap + next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Liz Hansen <liz.hansen@greenvault.com>, Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@greenvault.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: GreenVault discovery: reliability & graceful-degradation recap + next steps

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the candid discussion. Below is a short recap of what we heard, the success criteria you called out, immediate clarifying questions, and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Quick summary of pain points you shared
- Recurring inference outages over the last 6 months (impacting authorization flows and risk scoring).
- Manual failover to eu-west-1; region failover is slow and error-prone.
- Cost and latency are both concerns — you need predictable tail latency for interactive flows and lower unit cost for batch scoring.
- Audit and data residency constraints for certain PII workflows.

Current stack (as described)
- Self-hosted transformer endpoints (cust-managed autoscaling) running primary in us-east-1, a secondary region in eu-west-1 used for DR.
- Mix of model sizes: a 7B fine-tuned model for web interactions; a larger 70B for internal analytics.
- Prefix caching currently disabled; requests often re-run identical context.

Stated success criteria (to confirm)
- Availability: >= 99.9% for the interactive scoring endpoint.
- Latency: median token latency target ~200ms at target concurrency; tail (95th) requirement TBD.
- Recovery: automated graceful degradation — automated fallback to smaller model variant and region-level reroute with RTO < 30s (initial ask).
- Observability: token-level cost and per-request tracing, plus retention of audit logs for 12 months.

Incidents we discussed (high level)
- Customer-facing outage on 2026-02-14: long token generation times after cache eviction; manual rollback took ~1.5 hours.
- Capacity-related slowdown 2026-05-03 during a marketing event; autoscaler mis-scaling led to dropped requests.

Immediate clarifying questions (please confirm in reply)
1) Is the interactive scoring endpoint the highest-priority flow for availability?
2) You mentioned three incidents in the last 6 months — I captured two above; can you confirm dates?
3) What is your expected peak RPS and average request size (tokens in/out)?

Proposed next steps
1) Technical deep-dive (engineering-to-engineering) — 60m to go over model sizes, current autoscaler behavior, KV/prefix cache, and logs (propose Mon/Tue next week).
2) Two-week proof-of-concept: Redwood Dedicated pool with graceful-degradation policy enabled (automated small-model fallback + region failover) and SLO measurement.
3) Security/materials: we'll share a SOC2 summary and SLO playbook; please share any evidence checklist or questionnaire from your side.
4) Commercial: we can draft a mutual action plan (MAP) after the technical deep-dive to capture procurement timeline and data residency requirements.

Attachments sent with this recap: redwood-slo-playbook.pdf (SLO examples + fallback patterns), soc2-summary.pdf, gv-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (blank template).

Next call proposal: engineering deep-dive on Tue 2026-09-08 or Wed 2026-09-09 — I’ll send a calendar poll after your confirmation.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0189

From: Liz Hansen <liz.hansen@greenvault.com>

Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 20:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GreenVault discovery: reliability & graceful-degradation recap + next steps

Soojin — thanks for the clear write-up. A couple of quick corrections and clarifications from our side: 
- We actually logged three incidents in the last 6 months; the third was a partial degradation on 2026-06-17 when a model rollout caused increased latency for ~45 minutes.
- For RTO: we originally said <30s as an ideal; pragmatic target our SRE team would accept is <= 60s for automated failover (we can tighten after the PoC).
- Latency success criteria: 95th percentile under typical load should be <350ms for the interactive endpoint.
- Peak load: roughly 120 RPS during peak business hours; average requests ~30 RPS. Typical token payloads average 120 tokens in, 80 tokens out per request.
- Data residency: EU PII must remain in eu-west-1 — for those flows we need region-local processing.

Procurement note: we’re aiming to finish vendor selection by end of Q4. A clear MAP and cost estimate for the two-week PoC will help speed approvals.

Happy to take the technical deep-dive next Tue morning (09/08) — Rajiv and I prefer 10:00–12:00 PT window.

—Liz
Liz Hansen
Head of Infrastructure, GreenVault Financial
liz.hansen@greenvault.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GreenVault discovery: reliability & graceful-degradation recap + next steps

Quick E2E notes from my side (technical):
- Please confirm exact model families and parameter counts for the production endpoints (we need to size CPU/GPU KV caches appropriately).
- Do you use per-tenant encryption keys or a single key per cluster? KMS details will inform our private deployment spec.
- For the PoC we’ll want a 48–72 hour traffic replay (sanitized) and a short live soak at target concurrency (120 RPS) to validate failover behaviors and tail latency.
- Suggested initial Redwood config for PoC: continuous prefix/KV caching enabled, small-model fallback chain (7B -> 3B), region-based routing with health probes at 5s cadence, and automatic model fallback at 95th latency breach.
- We’ll also surface what logs/traces we need (token-level cost, request_id, kv_cache_hit, model_variant, latency_ms).

If GreenVault can share a short sample load profile and a sanitized trace from one incident, we can prepare a focused test plan before the deep-dive.

Rishi
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
